rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the back boundary at Song.8.5|8.6 is asserted with no tier-1 marker, and the rejected alternative never engages the stronger rival of folding 8:5's address half into the 8:6-7 epigram it grammatically matches. OL: the same seam is cut inside a continuous 2ms-address chain, with no tier-1 marker, no tier-3 corroboration and no disclosure of the straddle; secondarily, the attested ascent shape is narrower than the row's 3-verse mi-zot digit implies.
rulings.grounds: SAME defect, reached independently by both primaries, and it is upheld. Re-derived from bytes: MT 8:5's second half runs one 1cs speaker addressing one 2ms hearer four times - עֽוֹרַרְתִּ֔יךָ, חִבְּלַ֣תְךָ, אִמֶּ֔ךָ, יְלָדַֽתְךָ (oshb:Song.8.5, byte tier) - and the identical configuration continues past the cut in שִׂימֵ֨נִי with לִבֶּ֗ךָ and זְרוֹעֶ֔ךָ (oshb:Song.8.6, byte tier). Read off the pointed codepoints, all six second-person suffixes are final kaf plus qamats (2ms); no gendered form changes at the seam, so under the owner's moderate voice policy the cut carries no tier-1 marker and the picture across it is tier-2 continuity. The row's only cited seam evidence is the setumah closing MT 8:4, which brackets the row's FRONT; the mark layer places no seg at all between MT 8:4 and MT 8:7, so as tier-3 single-witness corroboration it brackets MT 8:5-8:7 as one block and argues against this cut rather than for it. A byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity against the row unless disclosed, and nothing in the row's prose discloses it. OL's secondary is REFUTED ON THE OBJECT and upheld only as a labelling defect: the row's device-note digit counts the mi-zot formula, and that object is byte-correct at 3 verses (skeleton sweep: oshb:Song.3.6, oshb:Song.6.10, oshb:Song.8.5); what is wrong is calling all three ascending-question sites, since the ascent run מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ מִן הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר is attested at only 2 of them (skeleton sweep: oshb:Song.3.6, oshb:Song.8.5) - oshb:Song.6.10 reads הַנִּשְׁקָפָ֖ה (byte tier) with no ascent language - so one citation blends two objects. Tier-4 note: no WEB speaker heading was relied on by either packet or by this ruling.
rulings.remedy: In boundary_rationale, add the back-seam disclosure: splice the straddling chain (עֽוֹרַרְתִּ֔יךָ ... יְלָדַֽתְךָ from oshb:Song.8.5; לִבֶּ֗ךָ and זְרוֹעֶ֔ךָ from oshb:Song.8.6, byte tier) and state that no gendered form changes at Song.8.5|8.6, so the cut rests on a speech-act change and is tier-2 at best; add oshb:Song.8.6 to boundary_evidence_refs and disclose that the mark layer places no seg between MT 8:4 and MT 8:7 (tier-3, single-witness). In strongest_rejected_alternative, replace the whole-verse lyric_address strawman with the live rival - folding 8:5b into the 8:6-7 epigram, i.e. a Song.8.5-Song.8.7 unit - keeping the one-sentence limit. In device_notes, re-cut the blended count: name the object as the mi-zot formula (sweep: 3 verses) and, if the ascent language is wanted, cite it as its own object (sweep: 2 verses). NEW (neither packet): the same rejected-alternative sentence appeals to the treatment used for the book's other ascending-question sites - a cross-row reference that is not verse-anchored, barred by the register rule; re-anchor it to the verses. TESTS the cure must pass: (1) no seam claim rests on a device that runs unbroken across it undisclosed; (2) every count citation names exactly one object; (3) every spliced run re-collates at byte tier. Any change to the Song.8.5|8.6 cut itself is a PROPOSAL requiring boss adoption, and it is ONE edit with the P02-018 front seam.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the row states no tier-1 warrant for its own front boundary at Song.8.5|8.6, the same 1cs/2ms address pattern running unbroken into 8:6 as an undisclosed cross-seam device. OL: the front seam is labelled a voice shift although speaker and addressee are unchanged across it - what changes is verbal mood - and the straddling address chain is undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Both primaries are byte-right, and this is the SAME seam as the P02-017 ruling (one edit, two rows). The bytes: שִׂימֵ֨נִי (oshb:Song.8.6, byte tier) is a masculine-singular imperative carrying a 1cs object suffix, so the speaker is still 1cs and the addressee still 2ms, exactly as at עֽוֹרַרְתִּ֔יךָ (oshb:Song.8.5, byte tier); the row's front-seam signal, naming a 2ms imperative address as a voice shift, therefore misdescribes what actually changes, which is mood and speech act. That much is an ordinary defect and would be upheld on its own. What is escalated is the consequence, because it turns on an owner-level precedence reading the packets cannot settle: the owner's own closed unit vocabulary names the 8:6-7 love-strong-as-death peak as an epigram_unit exemplar, which presupposes this very Song.8.5|8.6 cut, while the moderate voice policy supplies no tier-1 marker at it, the hybrid granularity rule bars cutting inside a sustained single-voice run without one, and the tier-3 layer brackets MT 8:5-8:7 as a single seg block (no mark between MT 8:4 and MT 8:7, single-witness). Candidate dispositions for the boss round: (a) ratify the cut and rule that a marked speech-act change plus the named epigram category is sufficient warrant at an unmarked seam, requiring the straddle to be disclosed and confidence held no higher than medium_low; or (b) rule the tier-1-marker requirement controlling and adopt a Song.8.5-Song.8.7 merge as the boundary proposal, which would absorb P02-017. Note that neither primary escalated; both treated this as a defect call, and the mislabel is curable either way while the cut's survival is not.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF and OL, independently: the gloss 'for love is strong as death' translates a word that falls outside the quoted Hebrew run - a quote/gloss same-span violation.
rulings.grounds: SAME defect in both packets; distinct from the seam item on this row. Verified from bytes: MT 8:6 reads כִּֽי immediately before עַזָּ֤ה כַמָּ֨וֶת֙ אַהֲבָ֔ה, and the row's spliced run begins at the adjective, re-collating at byte tier against oshb:Song.8.6; the attached gloss opens with 'for', which renders only the excluded particle. Engagement class, one-word cure. Credit where both packets converge and this peer confirms: the cluster's highest-risk item is handled correctly in the same field - the divided-token pair שַׁלְהֶ֥בֶתְ יָֽה re-collates at byte tier at oshb:Song.8.6, the one-word/divided-token fact and the lemma tag are disclosed, the construal is held rather than decided, and no standalone Yah digit is overclaimed (see supported_sample).
rulings.remedy: Re-cut the pair as ONE edit: either extend the spliced run to כִּֽי עַזָּ֤ה כַמָּ֨וֶת֙ אַהֲבָ֔ה (spliced from oshb:Song.8.6 and re-collated to byte tier) or drop 'for' from the gloss. TEST the cure must pass: every English gloss attached to a Hebrew run translates only what that run contains, and the re-spliced run re-collates at byte tier against its own cited ref.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL: the rival dialogue reading is rejected on a ground the bytes contest, and the book's only two wall-noun sites sit on either side of the row's own back seam, undisclosed. (LF supported this row.)
rulings.grounds: The load-bearing half is upheld; the framing half is corrected. UPHELD: חוֹמָ֣ה (oshb:Song.8.9) and חוֹמָ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.10) are the lexeme's only two sites in the book (skeleton sweep: 2 verses), they are adjacent, and they are identical only once cantillation is stripped (byte tier at each ref, accent_stripped tier as a pair). The answer is clause-for-clause: אִם חוֹמָ֣ה הִ֔יא is answered by אֲנִ֣י חוֹמָ֔ה, and וְשָׁדַ֖יִם אֵ֣ין לָ֑הּ is answered by וְשָׁדַ֖י כַּמִּגְדָּל֑וֹת (byte tier at their own refs). That byte-true device straddles the row's own back seam with nothing in the prose disclosing it, while web:Song.8.10-Song.8.12 sits in boundary_evidence_refs without ever being argued. REFINED: the challenge says the bytes contest the stated ground; they do not. 'One speaker-group without an answering party' is byte-true of the span's interior - oshb:Song.8.8 carries לָ֨נוּ֙, נַּעֲשֶׂה֙, לַאֲחֹתֵ֔נוּ and oshb:Song.8.9 carries נִבְנֶ֥ה and נָצ֥וּר, all 1cp, all byte tier. The corrected finding is that the rejected alternative engages the wrong rival: the live rival the bytes make available is a Song.8.8-Song.8.10 dialogue_exchange, not a Song.8.8-Song.8.9 one, and the row never reaches it. LF's support of this row is independently verified and not contradicted (see supported_sample): the 1cp front seam and the achot role-split are both sound, and the back seam survives the straddling device because the 1cp-to-1cs person change at oshb:Song.8.9|8.10 is in-verse and marked.
rulings.remedy: Disclose the straddling wall-noun and breast answer at the Song.8.9|8.10 seam in boundary_rationale, splicing both sides at byte tier and naming the tiers honestly (byte at each ref; identical only at accent_stripped tier as a pair), and state why the seam survives it - the marked 1cp-to-1cs person change. Replace the rejected alternative's rival with a Song.8.8-Song.8.10 dialogue_exchange, within the one-sentence limit. Either argue web:Song.8.10-Song.8.12 in prose or drop the ref. NEW (neither packet): the identification of the speaker-group AS the brothers is carried by content inference alone - no in-verse form names them - while the byte anchor that would carry it sits unused at oshb:Song.1.6, בְּנֵ֧י אִמִּ֣י (byte tier), the same verse that supplies the keeper-and-vineyard chain linking oshb:Song.1.6, oshb:Song.8.11 and oshb:Song.8.12 (skeleton sweep: 3 verses); cite it or lower the attribution's stated tier. TESTS the cure must pass: (1) no byte-true device straddles the row's seam undisclosed; (2) the rejected alternative names the strongest rival the bytes make available; (3) every attribution states the tier that carries it.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL: the quoted marker is a common-gender pronoun and cannot carry the row's return to her own voice, the verse's actual gender-bearing forms go unquoted, and the petuchah is placed inside the verse rather than at the division it closes. (LF supported this row, calling the pronoun an unambiguous tier-1 marker and the mark correctly disclosed.)
rulings.grounds: Upheld on both counts, and LF's support is refuted in part. אֲנִ֣י (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier) fixes person and number only; set against the 1cp נִבְנֶ֥ה and נָצ֥וּר of oshb:Song.8.9 (byte tier) it is genuine tier-1 evidence for a SPEAKER change, so the seam itself stands and LF is right that far - but the owner voice policy requires the gender-marked form to be quoted for the attribution, and this verse's gender-bearing forms sit unquoted inside it: כְּמוֹצְאֵ֥ת, a feminine-singular participle, בְעֵינָ֖יו, a 3ms suffix locating the other party as a man, and וְשָׁדַ֖י כַּמִּגְדָּל֑וֹת answering oshb:Song.8.8 (all byte tier). Second count, also upheld: the mark inventory is verse-keyed and this cluster's own rows read a seg as closing its verse - the setumah at MT 8:4 is cited as the front seam of Song.8.5, the setumah at MT 8:7 as the front seam of Song.8.8 - so the book's single petuchah at MT 8:10 corroborates the MT 8:10|8:11 division, which is this row's BACK seam, not the front seam the row attaches it to; and 'sitting exactly at this pronoun-marked return' is an intra-verse position claim a verse-keyed single-witness inventory cannot source. The 1-of-20 digit, the petuchah-versus-setumah distinction and the single-witness disclosure are correct, and the mark is not treated as the driver.
rulings.remedy: Splice כְּמוֹצְאֵ֥ת שָׁלֽוֹם and בְעֵינָ֖יו (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier) into the seam warrant so the attribution rests on a gender-marked form, keeping אֲנִ֣י as the person-and-number marker it actually is. Re-cut the parashah sentence to the division the seg closes (MT 8:10|8:11) and delete the intra-verse placement; the dependent signal key must move from a self-marker to a back-seam key, since the driver framing changed. Re-open confidence, which was set above its siblings on the strength of the marker now corrected. TESTS the cure must pass: (1) the row's voice-attribution claim quotes a gender-marked form at byte tier; (2) no parashah citation asserts an intra-verse position or is attached to a seam the seg does not touch; (3) the confidence band is re-derived after the driver change rather than carried over.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: boundary_rationale and boundary_evidence_refs name only the tier-3 petuchah at MT 8:10 as the stated front-seam evidence; the actual tier-1 warrant, the person shift from her 1cs declaration into 3ms narration naming Solomon, is disclosed only inside strongest_rejected_alternative.
rulings.grounds: Upheld, and DISTINCT from OL's item on this same row - LF's is a tier-discipline placement defect, OL's is a false person claim; they are not the same defect and both stand. The rationale's one explicit seam citation is the preceding verse's petuchah, tier-3 corroboration that may never be a driver, while the grammatical pivot is real and left out of the field where warrant is expected: אֲנִ֣י חוֹמָ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier) gives way to third-person narration כֶּ֣רֶם הָיָ֤ה לִשְׁלֹמֹה֙ with 3ms נָתַ֥ן and בְּפִרְי֖וֹ (oshb:Song.8.11, byte tier). Unlike P02-020, the mark is correctly PLACED here - a seg closing MT 8:10 does corroborate the MT 8:10|8:11 division - so the defect is that a tier-3 corroborator stands alone in the seam-warrant field, not that it is misapplied.
rulings.remedy: Move the person-shift warrant into boundary_rationale with byte-tier splices from oshb:Song.8.10 and oshb:Song.8.11, and demote the petuchah sentence to explicit corroboration (single-witness, tier-3, never the driver), freeing strongest_rejected_alternative for the rival within its one-sentence limit. NEW (neither packet): the same sentence appeals to the strategy's own vineyard-mashal category - a strategy-file citation barred from row prose by the register rule - so the replacement warrant must be argued from bytes, not from a category name. TEST the cure must pass: strike the tier-3 sentence and boundary_rationale must still carry a tier-1 seam warrant on its own bytes.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL: the claim that a 1cs possessive marks her voice throughout is false for MT 8:11, which carries no first-person form at all, and the 1cs forms in MT 8:12 are common-gender - the female attribution rests on cross-verse continuity alone.
rulings.grounds: Upheld; distinct from LF's item on this row. Re-derived: oshb:Song.8.11 carries no first-person form whatever - its finite verbs are הָיָ֤ה, נָתַ֥ן and יָבִ֥א, and its only person-marked suffix is 3ms בְּפִרְי֖וֹ (byte tier) - so 'throughout' overreaches by exactly the verse the row opens on. At oshb:Song.8.12 the run כָּרְמִ֥י שֶׁלִּ֖י לְפָנָ֑י is common-gender 1cs, and the verse's only person-marked address is 2ms לְךָ֙ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה (byte tier), which the possessive characterization drops entirely. Under the owner voice policy that leaves the female attribution resting on tier-2 cross-verse continuity, barred as a sole driver. OL's proposed byte anchor checks out and is better than the row's: the possessive phrase recurs at oshb:Song.1.6 as כַּרְמִ֥י שֶׁלִּ֖י - the phrase's only two sites (skeleton sweep: 2 verses) - matching at SKELETON tier only, since the first vowel differs, while oshb:Song.1.6 is unambiguously her voice (שֶׁאֲנִ֣י שְׁחַרְחֹ֔רֶת, נֹטֵרָ֣ה, byte tier), and the keeper lexeme links oshb:Song.1.6, oshb:Song.8.11 and oshb:Song.8.12 (skeleton sweep: 3 verses).
rulings.remedy: Rewrite the attribution: drop 'throughout', restrict the 1cs possessive claim to oshb:Song.8.12, and add לְךָ֙ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה as part of what that verse attests. Carry the female attribution on the oshb:Song.1.6 anchor, cited at SKELETON tier for the phrase pair - byte tier is unavailable there, the first vowel differs - together with the byte-tier feminine forms at oshb:Song.1.6, and add oshb:Song.1.6 to boundary_evidence_refs with the cross-row reference verse-anchored. TESTS the cure must pass: (1) no person or gender claim is asserted over a verse that does not attest the form; (2) every recurrence claim names the tier that carries it, and a skeleton-tier match is never written as verbatim; (3) the mirrored ref set covers every verse argued outside the row's own span.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the Hebrew quote excludes 'chaverim' yet the attached gloss translates it - a quote/gloss same-span violation. OL: the same parity defect, plus the row's warrant that gender marking is thin across both verses, which the bytes contest with the span's cleanest 2fs/2ms minimal pair and the policy's first-named tier-1 address word.
rulings.grounds: Two findings on one row: the parity defect is the SAME defect in both packets; OL's marker-thinness finding is DISTINCT and additional; both upheld. Parity: MT 8:13 reads חֲבֵרִ֛ים immediately before the row's run מַקְשִׁיבִ֥ים לְקוֹלֵ֖ךְ הַשְׁמִיעִֽינִי (re-collated: byte tier at oshb:Song.8.13), and 'companions' stands unbracketed in the gloss; the run is additionally mislabelled a 2fs imperative summons, since its first word מַקְשִׁיבִ֥ים is a masculine-plural participle agreeing with those companions - only הַשְׁמִיעִֽינִי is the feminine-singular imperative. Marker thinness: read off the pointed codepoints, לְקוֹלֵ֖ךְ (oshb:Song.8.13) ends final kaf plus sheva, the 2fs shape, and לְךָ֤ (oshb:Song.8.14) ends final kaf plus qamats, the 2ms shape - a byte-level minimal pair across the row's internal seam - alongside הַיוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת standing in vocative position, the masculine-singular imperatives בְּרַ֣ח and וּֽדְמֵה, and the explicit vocative דּוֹדִ֗י, the address word the owner voice policy names first. The digit for that address vocabulary is 24 verses in its attested exact spellings, and the object matters: a contiguous-consonant sweep returns 25 because it also catches דּוֹדִֽים at oshb:Song.5.1, which is the lovers-noun, not her address word - the five-object dod trap, avoided here. So the row's stated warrant, that the markers are too thin to argue a tier-1 seam, is contradicted by its own two verses; holding the pair as one dialogue_exchange stays defensible on the hold-whole ground, but on a different warrant and a re-derived confidence band. Tier-4: no WEB speaker heading is relied on by either packet or by this ruling, in either direction.
rulings.remedy: Re-cut the gloss to its run, or extend the run to include חֲבֵרִ֛ים and re-collate to byte tier, and drop the 2fs-imperative label from the masculine-plural participle. Replace the thin-markers warrant with the hold-whole warrant, quoting the לְקוֹלֵ֖ךְ against לְךָ֤ pair and דּוֹדִ֗י at byte tier and naming the address-vocabulary digit with its object (exact attested spellings, sweep: 24 verses). Re-open confidence, which was pinned to the misstatement. NEW (neither packet): the rejected alternative states that the strategy names this pair as one dialogue_exchange zone - a strategy-file citation barred from row prose by the register rule; re-argue the hold-whole ground from the verses themselves. TESTS the cure must pass: (1) every gloss translates only what its run contains; (2) each speaker turn names the verse it is marked in with the gender-marked form spliced at byte tier; (3) no digit is cited without naming the object swept.

The role-split and the 1cp front seam both hold. supported_sample.claim_checked: LF's support that the petuchah is correctly disclosed as tier-3 corroboration only and not the driver, and that the pronoun is an unambiguous tier-1 marker.
supported_sample.notes: Half verified, half refuted. Verified: the mark is disclosed single-witness, the petuchah-versus-setumah distinction holds, the 1-of-20 digit matches the inventory, and the row does not treat the mark as the driver. Refuted: the seg is verse-keyed and closes its verse, as this cluster's other rows themselves read it, so the mark corroborates the MT 8:10|8:11 division and not the front seam it is attached to, and 'sitting exactly at this pronoun-marked return' is an unsourceable intra-verse position claim; separately אֲנִ֣י is common-gender, so it cannot carry the attribution to her voice while כְּמוֹצְאֵ֥ת and בְעֵינָ֖יו (byte tier, same verse) go unquoted. This is the ruling entered for P02-020.

supported_sample.claim_checked: The claim both packets credited: that the divided-token pair is handled at byte tier with the one-word/divided-token fact disclosed, the construal held, and no standalone Yah digit overclaimed.
supported_sample.notes: שַׁלְהֶ֥בֶתְ יָֽה re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Song.8.6. The row's Yah-form digit names the right object: a whole-token sweep of the standalone form returns 1 verse, oshb:Song.8.6, whereas the naive contiguous-consonant sweep of the two-letter string returns 11 verses - the trap the row avoids. The accompanying absence digits also hold: the plain divine names return 0 verses each across all 117. The construal is held rather than decided and the exegesis note is marked single-witness apparatus.
